issues.detail: The Greek 'προεχειρισατο' (proexecharisato) means 'purposed' or 'intended' (from pro-ekcheirizō), but the Vietnamese 'đã chọn' means 'chose' or 'elected'. This changes the nature of the action from a divine purpose/plan to a specific act of selection.

The Greek phrase 'τον δικαιον' (ton dikaion) refers to 'the righteous' (singular or collective), but the Vietnamese 'Đấng Công Bình' (capitalized) implies a specific title/person ('The Righteous One') rather than the quality of being righteous.
